Add a real library failure case, catch the expected exception outside the instrumented call so telemetry flushes, and regenerate the results to demonstrate an ERROR retrieval span and a duration measurement with matching `error.type`. The span declaration at `model/gen-ai/spans.yaml:458` has the same coverage gap.

threads.body: `data_source_id` is only copied into arbitrary document metadata; it is not configured as an identifier on `InMemoryDocumentStore` or `InMemoryBM25Retriever`. Emitting it here therefore does not demonstrate a data-source ID available to generic Haystack instrumentation, as required by `.github/instructions/evaluate-reference.instructions.md:17-33`. Drop this attribute from the span, span name, and metric unless the scenario obtains an actual library-supported data-source identifier.

threads.body: `weather-knowledge-base` is application-defined document metadata, not a data-source identifier understood by `BaseRetriever.invoke`. The custom `WeatherRetriever` does not expose a data-source ID either, so this new metric dimension and sampling attribute are not backed by a library-defined input or state. Following `.github/instructions/evaluate-reference.instructions.md:17-33`, omit the ID from the span, span name, and metric, or use a retriever API that actually exposes one.

threads.body: The only consumer of `top_k` is the scenario's own `WeatherRetriever._get_relevant_documents` implementation, not a limit parameter defined and interpreted by LangChain. This does not demonstrate how generic LangChain instrumentation can obtain `gen_ai.retrieval.top_k`, as required by `.github/instructions/evaluate-reference.instructions.md:17-29`. Drop this emission or use a concrete library retriever with a native limit setting.

threads.body: This ID comes from the scenario's constant and arbitrary document `source_id` metadata, not from `VectorStoreIndex` or the retriever's identity/configuration. It therefore does not establish that LlamaIndex instrumentation can capture this data-source identifier at span creation. Per `.github/instructions/evaluate-reference.instructions.md:17-33`, drop it from the span, span name, and metric, or demonstrate an identifier the library actually exposes.
